payload.wgsl:
#param color SUNG #ffffff — what the sweep leaves behind
#param float DIM 0.66 0 1 — lines that are not being sung, 0..1.
#param float SWEEP 0.01 0 0.05 — how soft the wipe's edge is, in box widths

// Now Playing — the words as a scrolling column, the way a streaming app shows
// them: the whole track on screen at once, the line being sung bright, the rest
// receding, and the column easing upward as each line lands.
//
// A BACKGROUND, so the gradient replaces the world and the cast dances in
// front of the words. That is the vertical-video look this is for — the frame
// is a phone screen, the dancer is the subject, and the lyrics are the wall
// behind. (Rename `background` to `foreground` and it plays over the top
// instead, covering the scene.)
//
// The TEXT arrives from the host — pair an .lrc with the track (X.mp3 beside
// X.lrc) and every line is rasterised once into the lyric atlas. What this file
// owns is the column: where lines sit, how the scroll eases, and how the one
// being sung is told apart from the rest.
//
//   rzLyricCount()       lines in the track
//   rzLyricStart(i)      when line i lands, in track seconds
//   rzLyricText(i, uv)   glyph coverage of line i; uv is 0..1 across its box
//   rzLyricAspect(i)     the line's width over its height, as rasterised
//   rzLyricHasText(i)    false for a line that rasterised to nothing
//   rzLyricProgress(i,t) 0..1 through the line — the karaoke sweep

// Tunables — edit and ⌘⏎.

                                         // High enough to READ — the column is
                                         // the words of the song, and a line you
                                         // have to squint at is not showing them
const FOCUS = 1.1;                       // how tightly the highlight falls off
                                         // across neighbouring lines
// ── How the column is laid out ───────────────────────────────────────────
const TEXT_BIAS = 0.15;                  // how hard the WORDS lean on the frame's
                                         // shape. CARD_BIAS's gentler sibling —
                                         // see textK in words()
const LINE_H = 0.0388;                   // one line's height AT 9:16, fraction of
                                         // frame height — see sizeK in words()
const BIG = 1.0;                         // how much larger the sung line is set.
                                         // 1 is OFF: the line grows while the
                                         // whole column is moving, and two things
                                         // changing at once reads as busy
const STEP = 0.0644;                     // distance between lines, same units and
                                         // the same scaling — must exceed
                                         // LINE_H * BIG or lines collide
const MID = 0.50;                        // where the sung line sits, 0 bottom 1 top
const CEIL_FADE = 0.09;                  // the column fades out under the card
const FLOOR = 0.15;                      // and stops short of the bottom edge
const FLOOR_FADE = 0.12;
const XTILT = 0.0;                       // degrees tipped back about the horizontal
                                         // axis. 0 — the lines converging on one
                                         // horizon is cue enough, and the tip was
                                         // a second one competing with it
const CARD_GAP = 0.0186;                 // clearance between the card's lower edge
                                         // and the topmost line
const CARD_BIAS = 0.35;                  // HOW THE CARD SCALES with the frame.
                                         // 1 pins it to the frame's width, 0 to
                                         // its height; 0.5 is the geometric mean
                                         // of the two. Below 0.5 it leans toward
                                         // height, so a tall frame gets a bigger
                                         // card — which is the frame this look is
                                         // for, and 16:9 is the one it must not
                                         // shrink away on
const LEFT = 0.07;                       // left margin, fraction of frame width
const RIGHT = 0.07;                      // and the one the longest line stops at.
                                         // The column is SIZED to hold this — see
                                         // lineH in words() — so it is a margin
                                         // rather than a clip
const SPAN: i32 = 7;                     // lines drawn each way from the centre.
                                         // Enough to reach OFF the frame, now
                                         // that nothing fades them out before
                                         // they get there — a line that simply
                                         // stopped existing mid-frame would pop
                                         // once per scroll. The extra rows cost a
                                         // bounds test each and no more
const SCROLL = 0.70;                     // seconds the column takes to ease to
                                         // the next line — the whole feel of it
const TILT = 6.0;                        // degrees the column is turned about its
                                         // own vertical axis. The words stand at
                                         // the left FACING THE MIDDLE, so you
                                         // read them at an angle: the left edge
                                         // is nearest and each line recedes away
                                         // to the right.
                                         //
                                         // PURELY A LOOK, which it was not while
                                         // the column had no margin of its own:
                                         // the foreshortening was pulling the
                                         // longest line back inside the frame and
                                         // standing in for one. lineH does that
                                         // now, so this angle answers to nothing
                                         // but taste.
                                         //
                                         // What it does at each size. HORIZON and
                                         // MID are the same row, so the sung line
                                         // is level and the slope REVERSES across
                                         // it — lines above lean down toward it,
                                         // lines below lean up. At 6 that is 12%
                                         // of foreshortening at the frame's edge
                                         // on 9:16: a lean, read as the column
                                         // being set at an angle. Past about 20 it
                                         // reads as a wall in perspective, at the
                                         // cost of the far end of a long line.
                                         // Much past 60 is edge-on
const HORIZON = 0.50;                    // where the vanishing point sits up the
                                         // frame, 0 bottom 1 top.
                                         //
                                         // EVERY line converges toward this one
                                         // row, which is what makes them one
                                         // plane. A line here stays level; lines
                                         // above slope down toward it as they
                                         // recede and lines below slope up. Each
                                         // line converging on its OWN centre —
                                         // which is what scaling a fixed
                                         // centreline does — leaves them all
                                         // horizontal, and horizontal lines are
                                         // exactly what a turned plane does not
                                         // have
const DEPTH = 0.45;                      // how far away the column is, in FRAME
                                         // HEIGHTS — the same unit LINE_H is in,
                                         // and that is what makes the turn look
                                         // the same on every aspect.
                                         //
                                         // It was in frame WIDTHS, and a line's
                                         // reach along the plane is its own
                                         // width, which carries the aspect. So
                                         // the same line turned three times
                                         // harder on a vertical frame than on a
                                         // wide one, and on the wide one it was
                                         // 3% — a plane rotation nobody could
                                         // see, which is why it kept reading as
                                         // flat.
                                         //
                                         // Small is a wide-angle lens and a
                                         // violent turn; large flattens it
const SHARP = 0.35;                      // edge contrast; 0.5 is raw coverage,
                                         // lower is harder — under ~0.2 it steps
// The panel over the words, with the record turning on it. It is drawn in the
// SAME MOUNT — the card and the column are one wall standing behind the cast,
// on one plane, at one angle, and the dancer passes in front of all of it. That
// is what puts them in one file: they share the layout below, and a card whose
// left edge is the column's left edge cannot be a second effect.
const CY = 0.800;                        // and up it, 0 bottom 1 top
const CARD_W = 0.3784;                    // card size, in frame HEIGHTS — the same
                                         // unit a lyric line's height is in, so
                                         // the two keep their proportions to each
                                         // other on any aspect. Sized to
                                         // its CONTENTS: CONTENT_X + BAR_W +
                                         // one margin, where the margin is the
                                         // one the record keeps on the left
                                         // (REC_INSET - REC_R). It carried two
                                         // of them and sat 0.02 wide of its own
                                         // rule. Widen a row without widening
                                         // this and the padding on the right
                                         // goes with it
const CARD_H = 0.1399;
const CARD_R = 0.0314;                    // corner radius. At half the height it is
                                         // a pill; this is a rounded rectangle
                                         // that still reads as one
const GLASS = vec3f(1.0, 1.0, 1.0);      // the panel
const GLASS_A = 0.20;                    // how much of it there is, 0..1
const EDGE_A = 0.34;                     // the brighter hairline around it
const CARD_SHADOW = 0.11;                // what the card casts, 0 for none
const CARD_DROP = 0.0054;                 // how far below, in frame widths
const CARD_SOFT = 0.0236;                 // and how soft. Wider and fainter reads
                                         // as a panel lifted off the frame;
                                         // tighter and darker reads as a sticker

const REC_R = 0.0571;                     // record radius, frame widths
const REC_INSET = 0.0786;                 // its centre in from the card's left edge
const VINYL = vec3f(0.09, 0.09, 0.11);   // the disc
const LABEL = vec3f(0.88, 0.90, 0.94);   // the paper in the middle
const LABEL_R = 0.40;                    // as a fraction of the record's radius
const GROOVES = 240.0;                   // ring frequency across the disc
const SPIN = 0.15;                       // TURNS PER SECOND. A record does 0.55;
                                         // artwork on a lock screen turns far
                                         // slower, and slower still is what
                                         // reads as calm rather than busy
const SPIN_STOPS = 1.0;                  // 1: the disc turns only while the track
                                         // plays. 0: it turns regardless

// THE COLUMN BESIDE THE RECORD — three rows: spectrum, transport, progress.
// It had a third once before, a white bar standing in for a title, and a bar
// that says nothing is worse than the space it fills. This one says what the
// music is doing.
//
// EVERY ROW STARTS AT CONTENT_X, so the column has one left edge and the card
// has one margin after it. The rows are evenly spaced and the stack is centred,
// which is why these three numbers look arbitrary and are not: 0.016 of
// clearance between rows, and the same margin above the spectrum as below the
// progress bar. Move any row height and all three move.
const INK = vec3f(1.0, 1.0, 1.0);        // controls and the played bar
const CONTENT_X = 0.1599;                 // where the column starts, in from the
                                         // card's left edge
const ROW_EQ = 0.0143;                    // the spectrum STANDS ON this — it is a
                                         // baseline, where the two below are
                                         // centre lines
const ROW_CTL = -0.0089;                  // from the card's middle
const ROW_BAR = -0.0386;

const CTL_R = 0.0155;                     // control glyph size, frame widths
const CTL_GAP = 0.0431;                   // between one control and the next.
                                         // Scaled WITH CTL_R: hold the pitch
                                         // while the glyphs shrink and three
                                         // controls stop reading as one

const BAR_W = 0.197;                     // progress bar length, in frame widths —
                                         // it measures a song, it does not have
                                         // to reach the far edge to do it
const BAR_H = 0.0070;                    // and its thickness
const BAR_TRACK = 0.42;                  // the unplayed part's opacity. It has
                                         // to read as the same bar as the played
                                         // half, not as a groove behind it
const KNOB = 1.9;                        // the dot at the head, in bar heights.
                                         // 0 for a plain bar with no handle
// THE SPECTRUM, the row above the transport. rzAudioBand hands out the track's
// analysis already log-spaced and bass-first, which is the shape a meter wants
// — a column per slice of it, and no FFT to do here.
const EQ_BARS: i32 = 16;                 // columns, over BAR_W. The analysis
                                         // ships 32 bands, so each column is
                                         // exactly two of them; a count that
                                         // does not divide 32 gives some columns
                                         // more of the spectrum than others
const EQ_H = 0.031;                      // how tall a full-scale column stands,
                                         // in BAR_W's units
const EQ_FLOOR = 0.14;                   // what a silent column keeps, as a
                                         // fraction of EQ_H. A row of stubs
                                         // reads as a meter at rest; zero reads
                                         // as a card with something missing
const EQ_GAP = 0.34;                     // of each column's slice given to the
                                         // space beside it
const EQ_W = 0.85;                       // of BAR_W the strip reaches, from the
                                         // same left edge. Visibly short of the
                                         // bar below it, so the two rows read as
                                         // stacked rather than as one shape cut
                                         // in half
const EQ_ROUND = 0.35;                   // of a full pill each column's corners
                                         // take. 1 is a lozenge, 0 is a bar with
                                         // square ends
const EQ_A = 1.0;                        // how solid, against INK. Full, like
                                         // the transport and the played bar —
                                         // the column is a reading, not a hint,
                                         // and anything under 1 puts the panel's
                                         // own grey through it
// THE FALL. An analysed band is a number per frame with no memory, so a column
// driven straight off it flickers. These read a short way into the PAST and
// keep the loudest thing found, aged — fast to rise, slow to drop, which is
// what a level meter does and what makes a column look like it is falling
// rather than being redrawn.
const EQ_TAIL: i32 = 7;                  // samples of history
const EQ_STEP = 0.035;                   // seconds between them
const EQ_FALL = 2.2;                     // how fast a peak lets go, per second

const TRACK_LEN = 0.0;                   // seconds. 0 means TAKE IT FROM THE
                                         // LYRICS — the last line's end is what
                                         // the song is, for a card that exists to
                                         // sit beside them. Set it to override

/**
 * Ease 0..1, gentler than smoothstep at both ends.
 *
 * Smoothstep's second derivative is not zero where it starts and stops, so a
 * column moving under it sets off and arrives with a small kick — barely
 * visible in one move, unmistakable once it happens every line. This is the
 * quintic, flat to the second derivative at both ends, which is what makes a
 * scroll read as gliding rather than as being pushed.
 */
fn ease(x: f32) -> f32 {
  let u = clamp(x, 0.0, 1.0);
  return u * u * u * (u * (u * 6.0 - 15.0) + 10.0);
}

/**
 * The last line to have landed at t, or -1 before the first.
 *
 * BINARY, not a walk. This runs per pixel over the whole frame, and a track is
 * a hundred-odd lines — scanning them would be a hundred buffer reads for every
 * pixel of a 4K frame to answer a question with one answer. Eight steps covers
 * 256 lines, which is past the atlas cap.
 *
 * rzLyricIndex is the neighbouring question and the wrong one here: it returns
 * -1 BETWEEN lines, and a column that snapped back to nothing in every gap
 * between two sung lines is not a column.
 */
fn lineAt(t: f32) -> i32 {
  var lo = 0;
  var hi = rzLyricCount() - 1;
  var k = -1;
  for (var s = 0; s < 8; s = s + 1) {
    if (lo > hi) { break; }
    let mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
    if (rzLyricStart(mid) <= t) {
      k = mid;
      lo = mid + 1;
    } else {
      hi = mid - 1;
    }
  }
  return k;
}

/**
 * Glyph coverage over ONE SCREEN PIXEL, not at one point.
 *
 * The atlas holds a line at whatever size it was rasterised and the box is
 * drawn at whatever size the frame asks for, so the two rarely agree — and
 * where the atlas has more texels than the box has pixels, a single bilinear
 * tap simply misses some of them. That is what stair-steps a glyph edge. Four
 * taps on a rotated grid estimate the area, which is what an antialiased edge
 * actually is.
 */
fn coverage(i: i32, lu: vec2f, px: vec2f) -> f32 {
  var s = rzLyricText(i, lu + vec2f(0.125, 0.375) * px);
  s = s + rzLyricText(i, lu + vec2f(-0.375, 0.125) * px);
  s = s + rzLyricText(i, lu + vec2f(-0.125, -0.375) * px);
  s = s + rzLyricText(i, lu + vec2f(0.375, -0.125) * px);
  return s * 0.25;
}

/** Straight-alpha "over". The wall paints NOTHING of its own now, so every
 *  layer has to carry its own coverage and stack onto what is already there. */
fn over(dst: vec4f, src: vec3f, sa: f32) -> vec4f {
  let a = sa + dst.a * (1.0 - sa);
  if (a <= 1e-5) { return vec4f(0.0); }
  return vec4f((src * sa + dst.rgb * dst.a * (1.0 - sa)) / a, a);
}

/**
 * The scene's own mount for the words — BEHIND the cast, which is where they go.
 *
 * The column is laid out on the screen and turned by hand, which is where this
 * started and what looked right. A world-space plane hit by the camera's ray was
 * tried in between: it gave true perspective, parallax and depth for free, and
 * every version of it read wrong on screen. Correct and wanted are not the same
 * property, and this is the one that was wanted.
 */
fn background(ray: vec3f, uv: vec2f, time: f32) -> vec4f {
  // The card OVER the column, both behind the cast. The column already fades out
  // under the card — see CEIL_FADE — so this only settles the overlap at the
  // edge of that fade.
  let c = panel(uv);
  return over(words(uv), c.rgb, c.a);
}

fn words(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
  let res = rzResolution();
  let n = rzLyricCount();
  // NOTHING BEHIND THE WORDS. This used to paint a gradient wall and fill the
  // frame; now it is the words alone, so whatever the scene already has —
  // a backdrop, a skybox, a stage — is what they sit on.
  var out = vec4f(0.0);
  if (n == 0) { return out; }

  let t = rzAudioTime();
  let k = lineAt(t);
  // WHERE THE COLUMN IS, as a fractional line index. Easing from k-1 to k means
  // the column is still showing the previous line centred at the instant the
  // new one lands, and travels to it — which is why it reads as following the
  // song rather than cutting to it.
  var scroll = -1.0;
  if (k >= 0) {
    scroll = f32(k) - 1.0 + ease((t - rzLyricStart(k)) / SCROLL);
  }

  // THE TURN, once for the whole column — a plane rotated about its own
  // vertical axis, so its far edge foreshortens and its near edge opens out.
  let rad = radians(TILT);
  let cs = cos(rad);
  let sn = sin(rad);
  // And the tip. Its sine is how much a line's DEPTH changes per unit up the
  // column, its cosine how much of its height survives the tip on screen.
  let radx = radians(XTILT);
  let csx = cos(radx);
  let snx = sin(radx);
  // Frame heights to the units a line's width is in — bw carries this factor,
  // so anything mixed with a depth has to carry it too.
  let ar = res.y / max(res.x, 1.0);
  // THE SIZE, THROUGH THE LAW THE CARD IS DRAWN BY. LINE_H alone is a fraction
  // of frame HEIGHT, so text set for a tall export comes out small against a
  // wide one — the same drift the card leans away from with CARD_BIAS. Sharing
  // the law is also what keeps the two locked: the card's width and the words'
  // height move together when the aspect changes, instead of one growing while
  // the other stands still.
  //
  // LINE_H and STEP are therefore set for 9:16, which is what this look is for,
  // and every wider frame scales UP from there.
  let sizeK = pow(1.0 / max(ar, 1e-4), CARD_BIAS);
  // The WORDS lean the same way on a FLATTER curve. Sharing the card's exponent
  // outright overshot: a panel has to hold its controls at a legible size, so it
  // grows steeply off a tall frame, and type carried along at that rate came out
  // oversized on 16:9. TEXT_BIAS is the same law at a gentler slope — the two
  // still move together, just not by the same amount.
  let textK = pow(1.0 / max(ar, 1e-4), TEXT_BIAS);

  // THE COLUMN FITS THE FRAME, and LINE_H is the CEILING rather than the size.
  //
  // A line's width on screen is its height times its own proportions times
  // res.y/res.x, so it is tied to the frame's SHAPE and not to its width: at one
  // setting of LINE_H the longest line ran off the right edge of a 9:16 frame and
  // covered a third of a 2.39:1 one. The turn was hiding it — foreshortening
  // pulled the overrun back inside and looked like a margin — which is why
  // setting TILT to zero made the frame feel wrong rather than flat.
  //
  // rzLyricWidest is the longest line in the TRACK, packed by the host. Reading
  // every rect here would be a hundred buffer reads at every pixel of a 4K frame
  // to answer something that changes only when the song does; this is one.
  //
  // The cap is on the WHOLE COLUMN, never on the line that tripped it. Sizing
  // each line to its own width sets a verse smaller than the interjection above
  // it, for a reason the reader cannot see. 0 means the lines are not rasterised
  // yet, and a cap from that would be a cap on nothing.
  var lineH = LINE_H * textK;
  let widest = rzLyricWidest();
  if (widest > 0.0) { lineH = min(lineH, (1.0 - LEFT - RIGHT) / max(widest * ar, 1e-4)); }
  // The leading comes down with the type, so the column keeps its proportions
  // instead of opening out every time a wordy track brings the size down.
  let lead = STEP * textK * (lineH / max(LINE_H * textK, 1e-6));

  // WHERE THE CARD ENDS, through the same scale the card is drawn at — see the
  // note in `foreground`.
  //
  // `k`, not its reciprocal. This read sqrt(res.y/res.x) where the card is
  // drawn at sqrt(res.x/res.y) — the two are inverses, so the ceiling was out by
  // the square of the aspect and sat far below the card on a tall frame,
  // fading lines that had nothing above them.
  let ceil = CY - (CARD_H * 0.5 + CARD_GAP) * sizeK;

  let centre = i32(floor(scroll + 0.5));
  for (var o = -SPAN; o <= SPAN; o = o + 1) {
    let j = centre + o;
    if (j < 0 || j >= n) { continue; }
    if (!rzLyricHasText(j)) { continue; }

    // WHERE THIS LINE SITS ON THE TIPPED PLANE.
    //
    // sv is its place up the column before any projection; the tip turns that
    // into a depth, and the depth into both a screen position and a size. Lines
    // above the sung one are further away, so they draw closer together AND
    // smaller — the convergence is the whole point of the tip, and it comes out
    // of one perspective divide rather than being faked with two curves.
    let sv = (scroll - f32(j)) * lead;
    let dvn = DEPTH + sv * snx;
    // Past the camera. Only reachable at a steep tip with a long column, and
    // drawing it would fold the far end of the plane back over the near end.
    if (dvn < 1e-4) { continue; }
    let pv = DEPTH / dvn;
    let yc = MID + sv * csx * pv;
    // THE CEILING — the card is a solid panel and words sliding under it would
    // be words you cannot read. Faded rather than clipped, or a line would pop
    // out of existence once per scroll.
    let clear = (1.0 - smoothstep(ceil - CEIL_FADE, ceil, yc)) * smoothstep(FLOOR, FLOOR + FLOOR_FADE, yc);
    if (clear <= 0.0) { continue; }

    let away = abs(f32(j) - scroll);
    let near = clamp(1.0 - away * FOCUS, 0.0, 1.0);
    // TWO STYLES, and nothing between them: the line being sung, and every other
    // line. There is no fade with distance — a gradient down the column was
    // information nobody was reading, and it made a line you heard a minute ago
    // dimmer than one you heard a moment ago for no reason a listener could
    // name.
    //
    // `near` is not a distance fade. It is only wide enough to cross ONE line,
    // so all it does is hand the highlight over while the column is travelling
    // — at rest exactly one line is lit and the rest are at params.DIM.
    let lit = mix(params.DIM, 1.0, near * near) * clear;
    if (lit <= 0.0) { continue; }

    // EVERY LINE THE SAME SIZE. Its height is lineH and nothing else; only its
    // WIDTH follows from the rasterised proportions, so a long line is a long
    // line rather than a smaller one. What decides lineH — including the cap
    // that makes the longest line fit — is settled once, for the whole column,
    // above.
    //
    // This used to shrink whatever did not fit, per line, and the result was a
    // verse set smaller than the two-word interjection above it: type that
    // changes size down the page for reasons the reader cannot see.
    let bh = lineH * mix(1.0, BIG, near * near);
    let bw = bh * rzLyricAspect(j) * ar;

    // THE BAND THIS LINE CAN REACH, which is not the box it would occupy flat.
    //
    // Its centre travels toward the horizon along its own length, so a long
    // line far from the horizon ends up well outside that box — and rejecting
    // on the box alone chopped the far end off exactly those lines, which is
    // what the cut-off words were. The reject also had to move below bw: it
    // cannot know how far a line reaches until it knows how long the line is.
    let perspFar = dvn / max(dvn + (bw / ar) * sn, 1e-4);
    let reach = bh * pv * 1.6 + abs(yc - HORIZON) * (1.0 - perspFar);
    if (abs(uv.y - yc) > reach) { continue; }

    // BACK THROUGH THE TURN, about the COLUMN'S LEFT EDGE — one axis for every
    // line, which is what makes it one plane rather than a fan, and what keeps
    // the left margin a margin.
    let a2 = bw * cs;
    // WHICH WAY IT FACES, and this is the whole difference between a turn and a
    // foreshortening. b2 is POSITIVE, so depth GROWS along the line: the left
    // edge is nearest and each line recedes away to the right.
    //
    // That is what facing the middle means for a panel standing at the left of
    // frame — its normal points inward, so you read along it from its near
    // side. Negated, as this was, the panel faces AWAY from the middle: the
    // right end comes toward you and simply looks bigger, which is flat text
    // that grows rather than text on a turned plane.
    //
    // It is also the safe sign. With depth increasing along the line the
    // denominator can only grow, so the vanishing point is never on the piece
    // being drawn.
    let b2 = bw * sn;
    // The plane's distance, in the units this line is measured in. bw already
    // carries the aspect — a line's width is its height times its proportions
    // times res.y/res.x — so giving the distance the same factor makes the
    // ratio b2/depth aspect-free, and the turn is the same turn whether the
    // export is 16:9 or 9:16.
    // THIS LINE'S depth, not the column's: a line further up the tipped plane is
    // further away, so it turns from further away too. One plane, or the tip and
    // the turn would each be describing a different surface.
    let depth = dvn * ar;
    let dx = uv.x - LEFT;
    let den = a2 * depth - dx * b2;
    if (den < 1e-5) { continue; }
    let u = dx * depth / den;
    if (u < -0.02 || u > 1.02) { continue; }
    let persp = depth / max(depth + u * b2, 1e-4);
    // THE LINE SLOPES, and this is the whole of what was wrong.
    //
    // Projecting a plane, screen_y = f·Y / (D + s·sin) — the denominator grows
    // as you travel along the line, so the far end sits nearer the HORIZON. The
    // old form scaled the height about a fixed yc, which keeps every line
    // perfectly level and only makes the glyphs smaller: type being squashed,
    // not type on a turned surface. A turned plane has no horizontal lines on
    // it at all unless they lie on the horizon.
    //
    // So the line's own centre is projected too — pulled toward HORIZON by the
    // same persp that shrinks it — and the inverse below reads a pixel back to
    // where it lands on the plane.
    let planeY = (uv.y - HORIZON) / persp;
    // pv is what the tip did to this line, and it is already inside yc.
    let lu = vec2f(u, (planeY - (yc - HORIZON)) / (bh * pv) + 0.5);
    if (lu.y < -0.2 || lu.y > 1.2) { continue; }

    let sung = rzLyricProgress(j, t);
    let wipe = mix(-params.SWEEP, 1.0 + params.SWEEP, sung);

    let px = vec2f(1.0 / max(bw * persp * res.x, 1.0), 1.0 / max(bh * persp * res.y, 1.0));
    let glyph = smoothstep(0.5 - SHARP, 0.5 + SHARP, coverage(j, lu, px));

    // ONE COLOUR IN THE WHOLE COLUMN. The sweep is a change in BRIGHTNESS, not a
    // second ink.
    //
    // The part of the live line still to come is the same thing as a line that
    // has not arrived yet, so it is drawn the same way: params.SUNG at params.DIM, exactly
    // what every other line sits at. Giving it a colour of its own made three
    // greys on screen — heard, being heard, and not yet — when there are only
    // two states worth showing.
    //
    // The wipe belongs to the live line alone. rzLyricProgress answers for every
    // line, and reading it everywhere put the lines behind at full and the lines
    // ahead at nothing, which is the same mistake one level up.
    var amt = lit;
    if (j == k) {
      let played = 1.0 - smoothstep(wipe - params.SWEEP, wipe + params.SWEEP, lu.x);
      amt = mix(params.DIM, 1.0, played);
    }
    out = over(out, params.SUNG, glyph * amt);
  }
  return out;
}

/** Distance to a rounded box — negative inside. The one primitive the whole
 *  card is built from, corners and bars alike. */
fn sdBox(p: vec2f, b: vec2f, r: f32) -> f32 {
  let q = abs(p) - b + vec2f(r);
  return length(max(q, vec2f(0.0))) + min(max(q.x, q.y), 0.0) - r;
}

/**
 * Coverage of a shape whose distance is d, antialiased over one pixel.
 *
 * ONE MINUS a rising ramp, not a falling one. `smoothstep(px, -px, d)` reads as
 * the obvious way to write it, and WGSL leaves edge0 > edge1 UNDEFINED.
 *
 * The pixel comes from the caller rather than from fwidth, which is not
 * reliable in the branchy code below.
 */
fn fill(d: f32, px: f32) -> f32 {
  return 1.0 - smoothstep(-px, px, d);
}

/**
 * A transport triangle at `t`, pointing left when `dir` is -1 and right at +1,
 * spanning ±w and ±h at its base.
 *
 * Two half-planes and a pair of caps rather than an SDF — exact enough at this
 * size and far cheaper.
 *
 * WIDTH AND HEIGHT SEPARATELY, which is the whole reason this signature is not
 * one radius. It was, with the height falling out of the width through a fixed
 * slope, so the wedge stood 12% taller than the pause bars beside it and the
 * skip controls read as the larger pair. Glyphs in one row share a cap height;
 * only what they have to be wide can differ.
 *
 * CENTRED ON ITS OWN ORIGIN. It used to run from −0.18r to +0.5r, so its middle
 * sat a sixth of a glyph off where it was placed — which is most of why three
 * evenly-anchored controls came out unevenly spaced. The apex is where the
 * wedge closes, at +x, so dir −1 closes toward −t.x and points LEFT.
 */
fn tri(t: vec2f, dir: f32, w: f32, h: f32, px: f32) -> f32 {
  let x = t.x * dir;
  return fill(max(abs(t.y) - (w - x) * h / (2.0 * w), -x - w), px);
}

fn panel(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
  let res = rzResolution();
  let aspect = res.y / max(res.x, 1.0);
  // THE CARD IS SIZED BY THE GEOMETRIC MEAN OF THE FRAME'S SIDES.
  //
  // Neither dimension alone works, and both were tried. Frame WIDTHS drifted
  // against the words: a lyric line's width is its height times the line's
  // proportions times res.y/res.x, so the text opens out as the frame gets
  // taller and a card measured across the frame does not — on a vertical export
  // the words ran wide and the card sat small beside them. Frame HEIGHTS fixed
  // that and broke the other end: a 16:9 frame is short, so everything tied to
  // its height came out small on the format most people preview in.
  //
  // A power of the aspect sits between the two — CARD_BIAS picks where. At 0.5
  // it is the geometric mean, sqrt(res.x·res.y), and the card is the same
  // number of pixels in either orientation; below that a tall frame gets the
  // larger card, which is what this look is composed for.
  let k = pow(1.0 / max(aspect, 1e-4), CARD_BIAS);
  // Isotropic: x by the aspect, y alone, then both by the same k. Equal extents
  // here are equal extents in pixels, so a circle is a circle and a corner
  // radius is one number.
  var out = vec4f(0.0);

  let pScreen = vec2f(uv.x / max(aspect, 1e-4), uv.y) / k;
  // ANCHORED TO THE LEFT MARGIN rather than centred on a coordinate of its own,
  // so the card's left edge lands exactly where the column's does at every
  // aspect instead of only at the one it was tuned on.
  let c = vec2f(LEFT / max(aspect, 1e-4) / k + CARD_W * 0.5, CY / k);
  let half = vec2f(CARD_W * 0.5, CARD_H * 0.5);

  // ── The same turn the words are on ───────────────────────────────────
  //
  // ONE ANGLE, shared: TILT turns the card and the column alike, about an axis
  // at the same left margin, so they read as one plane standing in the frame
  // rather than as a flat card in front of turned text.
  //
  // The point is un-projected ONCE, here, and everything below is drawn on the
  // flat card as before — panel, record, controls, bar all turn together
  // because none of them knows it happened. Turning them one at a time would be
  // a rig of pieces that agree, which is not the same thing as a plane.
  //
  // The record becomes an ellipse on screen, which is what a circle on a turned
  // plane looks like.
  // THE SAME PLANE, not a parallel one.
  //
  // DEPTH is in frame heights and this space is frame heights over k, so the
  // card's distance is DEPTH/k — the identical surface the words stand on,
  // stated in the card's own units. It had a CARD_DEPTH of its own, and two
  // depths is two planes: they turned by the same angle and still would not
  // line up, because nothing made them the same distance away.
  let cardDepth = DEPTH / max(k, 1e-4);
  let sinT = sin(radians(TILT));
  let dxc = pScreen.x - (c.x - half.x);
  let denc = CARD_W * cos(radians(TILT)) * cardDepth - dxc * CARD_W * sinT;
  if (denc < 1e-5) { return out; }
  let uc = dxc * cardDepth / denc;
  let perspc = cardDepth / max(cardDepth + uc * CARD_W * sinT, 1e-4);
  // AND THE SAME HORIZON. The card converges where the lines do, so the whole
  // composition has one vanishing point. About its own centre — as this was —
  // the card stays level while every line slopes, and the two read as separate
  // surfaces that happen to be tilted alike.
  let horc = HORIZON / max(k, 1e-4);
  let p = vec2f(c.x - half.x + uc * CARD_W, horc + (pScreen.y - horc) / perspc);
  // One screen pixel in these units.
  let px = 1.0 / max(res.y * k, 1.0);

  let rel = p - c;
  let card = sdBox(rel, half, CARD_R);
  // Reject early and generously: the shadow reaches below and outside the card,
  // and everything past that is the great majority of the frame.
  if (card > CARD_DROP + CARD_SOFT * 2.0 + 0.01) { return out; }

  var col = vec3f(0.0);
  // THE SHADOW FIRST, and outside the panel only — a translucent panel with its
  // own shadow under it comes out muddy, because the shadow shows through the
  // thing casting it.
  let sd = sdBox(rel + vec2f(0.0, CARD_DROP), half, CARD_R);
  let inside = fill(card, px);
  var a = CARD_SHADOW * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, CARD_SOFT, sd)) * (1.0 - inside);
  if (inside <= 0.0) { return over(out, col, clamp(a, 0.0, 1.0)); }

  // The panel. No blur behind it — a foreground cannot read the pixel it is
  // covering, so this is honest translucency rather than frosted glass, which
  // over a photographic background is most of the way there anyway.
  col = GLASS;
  a = mix(a, GLASS_A, inside);
  // A hairline just inside the edge, which is what makes a translucent panel
  // read as a panel rather than as a smudge.
  let rim = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 2.0 * px, abs(card + px * 1.5));
  a = max(a, rim * EDGE_A * inside);

  // ── The record ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  let rc = c + vec2f(-half.x + REC_INSET, 0.0);
  let q = p - rc;
  let r = length(q);
  if (r < REC_R + px * 2.0) {
    let disc = fill(r - REC_R, px);
    // Grooves are CONCENTRIC, so they do not turn — a record's rings look still
    // while it spins, and animating them reads as a target rather than a disc.
    let groove = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(r * GROOVES);
    var rcol = VINYL * (0.86 + 0.30 * groove);
    // A fixed specular arc: the light in the room does not turn with the
    // record, so this stays where it is.
    let ang = atan2(q.y, q.x);
    rcol = rcol + vec3f(0.35) * pow(max(cos(ang - 0.9), 0.0), 6.0) * smoothstep(0.2, 1.0, r / REC_R);
    // THE TURN, on the TRACK's clock rather than the effect's — so a paused
    // scene is a paused record, and a scrub takes the disc back with it.
    let running = select(1.0, rzAudioPlaying(), SPIN_STOPS > 0.5);
    let spin = rzAudioTime() * SPIN * 6.2831853 * running;
    let lr = REC_R * LABEL_R;
    let label = fill(r - lr, px);
    rcol = mix(rcol, LABEL, label);
    // One asymmetric mark is all it takes to read as turning; a symmetric disc
    // looks still however fast it goes.
    //
    // CLOCKWISE, and the minus sign is the whole of it. uv arrives origin
    // bottom-left, so this space has y UP and an angle that grows sweeps
    // counter-clockwise — which is the way no record has ever turned. Written
    // without it the disc ran backwards, at the right speed, which is the sort
    // of wrong that survives every check but a second look.
    let notch = q - vec2f(cos(-spin), sin(-spin)) * lr * 0.55;
    rcol = mix(rcol, VINYL, fill(length(notch) - lr * 0.16, px) * label);
    rcol = mix(rcol, vec3f(0.0), fill(r - lr * 0.13, px));
    col = mix(col, rcol, disc);
    a = max(a, disc * inside);
  }

  // ── The column beside it: transport over progress ──────────────────────
  let x0 = c.x - half.x + CONTENT_X;

  // Back, pause, forward — a whole transport rather than two glyphs and a gap.
  //
  // THREE ANCHORS, ONE PITCH, each glyph centred on its own. Placing them by
  // where their first shape starts is what made the gaps uneven: a rewind is
  // two triangles and a pause is two bars, they are not the same width, and
  // hanging both off a left edge puts their middles in different places.
  let cy = c.y + ROW_CTL;
  var ctl = 0.0;
  for (var g = 0; g < 3; g = g + 1) {
    let gx = x0 + CTL_R * 0.64 + f32(g) * CTL_GAP;
    if (g == 1) {
      ctl = max(ctl, fill(sdBox(p - vec2f(gx - CTL_R * 0.26, cy), vec2f(CTL_R * 0.12, CTL_R * 0.46), CTL_R * 0.06), px));
      ctl = max(ctl, fill(sdBox(p - vec2f(gx + CTL_R * 0.26, cy), vec2f(CTL_R * 0.12, CTL_R * 0.46), CTL_R * 0.06), px));
    } else {
      // SKIP, not scan: one wedge against a stop bar, |< and >|. Two wedges is
      // rewind and fast-forward — a control for holding down, which is not what
      // sits either side of a play button on anything made this decade.
      //
      // -1 back, +1 forward, and the bar goes on the OUTSIDE: the wedge closes
      // against it, which is the whole picture — a track running into its own
      // end. The offsets put the pair's combined span at ±0.5r so the glyph is
      // centred on gx like the pause is.
      // 0.46 is the PAUSE BAR'S half-height, shared: three glyphs on one row
      // stand to one line. The offsets follow from the two half-widths — 0.30
      // and 0.12 — so the pair spans ±0.45 either side of gx and clears itself
      // by 0.06.
      let dir = select(1.0, -1.0, g == 0);
      let bar = vec2f(gx + dir * CTL_R * 0.33, cy);
      ctl = max(ctl, fill(sdBox(p - bar, vec2f(CTL_R * 0.12, CTL_R * 0.46), CTL_R * 0.06), px));
      ctl = max(ctl, tri(p - vec2f(gx - dir * CTL_R * 0.15, cy), dir, CTL_R * 0.30, CTL_R * 0.46, px));
    }
  }
  col = mix(col, INK, ctl);
  a = max(a, ctl * inside);

  // ── The spectrum: the top row, the progress bar's width ────────────────
  let bands = rzAudioBandCount();
  if (EQ_BARS > 0 && bands > 0) {
    let span = BAR_W * EQ_W;
    let u = (p.x - x0) / span;
    if (u >= 0.0 && u <= 1.0) {
      // ONE COLUMN PER PIXEL, found rather than searched: the slices tile the
      // row, so the pixel's own slice is the only one whose column can reach it
      // — its antialiased edge included, since the gap keeps the column clear of
      // the slice's sides.
      let b = clamp(i32(u * f32(EQ_BARS)), 0, EQ_BARS - 1);
      // The LOUDEST band in the column's slice, not the first one in it. Picking
      // one drops the rest: at 16 columns over 32 bands that is every other band
      // of the track never reaching the card.
      let lo = (b * bands) / EQ_BARS;
      let hi = max(((b + 1) * bands) / EQ_BARS, lo + 1);
      var v = 0.0;
      for (var s = 0; s < EQ_TAIL; s = s + 1) {
        let age = f32(s) * EQ_STEP;
        let decay = max(1.0 - age * EQ_FALL, 0.0);
        for (var i = lo; i < hi; i = i + 1) {
          v = max(v, rzAudioBandAt(i, -age) * decay);
        }
      }
      let h = (EQ_FLOOR + (1.0 - EQ_FLOOR) * clamp(v, 0.0, 1.0)) * EQ_H;
      let pitch = span / f32(EQ_BARS);
      let bx = x0 + (f32(b) + 0.5) * pitch;
      let bw = pitch * (1.0 - EQ_GAP) * 0.5;
      // STANDING ON its baseline, growing up. A meter has a floor; centred on a
      // row, the columns would grow both ways out of nothing.
      let base = c.y + ROW_EQ;
      let bar = fill(sdBox(p - vec2f(bx, base + h * 0.5), vec2f(bw, h * 0.5), min(bw, h * 0.5) * EQ_ROUND), px);
      col = mix(col, INK, bar * EQ_A);
      a = max(a, bar * EQ_A * inside);
    }
  }

  // ── How far through the track ──────────────────────────────────────────
  //
  // THE LENGTH COMES FROM THE WORDS unless it is set. The engine hands an
  // effect the audio's clock but not its duration, and a bar that guessed would
  // be a bar that lies — the last lyric's end is a length this card can
  // actually know, and this card exists to sit beside the lyrics.
  var span = TRACK_LEN;
  let n = rzLyricCount();
  if (span <= 0.0 && n > 0) { span = rzLyricEnd(n - 1); }
  if (span > 0.0) {
    let by = c.y + ROW_BAR;
    let played = clamp(rzAudioTime() / span, 0.0, 1.0);
    let x1 = x0 + BAR_W;
    let head = mix(x0, x1, played);
    let track = fill(sdBox(p - vec2f((x0 + x1) * 0.5, by), vec2f((x1 - x0) * 0.5, BAR_H * 0.5), BAR_H * 0.5), px);
    col = mix(col, INK, track * BAR_TRACK);
    a = max(a, track * BAR_TRACK * inside);
    // The played part, clipped to the track so its ends keep the same radius.
    let done = fill(
      sdBox(p - vec2f((x0 + head) * 0.5, by), vec2f(max((head - x0) * 0.5, BAR_H * 0.5), BAR_H * 0.5), BAR_H * 0.5),
      px,
    ) * track;
    col = mix(col, INK, done);
    a = max(a, done * inside);
    if (KNOB > 0.0) {
      let knob = fill(length(p - vec2f(head, by)) - BAR_H * KNOB * 0.5, px);
      col = mix(col, INK, knob);
      a = max(a, knob * inside);
    }
  }

  return over(out, col, clamp(a, 0.0, 1.0));
}
